By Zachary Cohen - September 19, 2026 78911 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 2 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 2 NFL best bets and Week 2 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Philadelphia Eagles at Tennessee Titans – 1:00 pm ET Last week, Barkley rushed for 83 yards on only 15 carries in a win over the Commanders. Now, the star faces a Titans team that allowed 142 yards on 32 carries against the Jets duo of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen. In that game, Tennessee’s Rush EPA/Play Allowed was -0.038, which was right around the -0.043 mark the team posted in 2025. All offseason long, we talked about Robert Saleh shaping up this defense, but there is a chance he won’t be successful in doing so. That said, this might just be a strong matchup for an elite rusher. Barkley is averaging 96.9 rushing yards per game in his last 30 games, and he has rushed for at least 78 yards in five of his last six games. Also, since signing with the Eagles, Barkley is averaging 100.4 rushing yards per game when Philly is favored by between 5.5 and 8 points. I just don’t see any reason he can’t get going in this game, and I’ll throw out the fact that the game script could really favor him. If the Eagles go up early, they’ll begin to rely on the run. Bet: Saquon Barkley Over 75.5 Rushing Yards (-135) & Alt Rushing Yards 100+ (+233 – 0.25 units) Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears – 1:00 pm ET I tweeted during last week’s game that I can’t understand how Wentz is the backup over JJ McCarthy, but that’s neither here nor there. Wentz went on to do just fine in a win over the Packers, and I don’t see the Vikings being shy about throwing the ball here. With the Bears having put 59 points on the Panthers, there’s just no way of standing a chance against them without making plays in the passing game. And if Bryce Young can go for 361 passing yards against this defense, you’d think Wentz can reach 225 with all of the weapons he has at his disposal. Also, the absence of Jordan Mason only makes it more likely that Kevin O’Connell will let Wentz cook — even if he’s doing it with a microwave. Wentz only threw for 133 yards in relief of an injured Kyler Murray lat week, but he also threw for at least 236 yards in three of his final four appearances in 2025. Two of those three games featured him throwing for over 300 yards. I’m not sure the result of this game will be pretty for Minnesota, but I see Wentz putting up a pretty decent yardage total. I actually really wanted to get more aggressive with this, but the pricing wasn’t great. Bet: Carson Wentz Over 224.5 Passing Yards (+127) Jacksonville Jaguars at Denver Broncos – 4:05 pm ET Is this a massive overreaction from Week 1? While the Jaguars absolutely pounded the Browns, the Broncos looked lousy in a 31-10 loss against the Chiefs. However, looking back to a year ago, Denver was a better football team than Jacksonville. Also, the Broncos had a better offseason than the Jaguars. So, while things did look ugly offensively last week, I’m chalking it up to a weird game. I don’t think anyone should be sounding the alarms on Davis Webb running the offense, and I feel good about Denver bouncing back at home. Under Sean Payton, the Broncos are 4-1 both straight-up and against the spread in home games with totals of 45.5 or higher. Denver also happens to be 6-1 both SU and ATS after scoring 14 or fewer points in its previous game. Those trends support a much better performance from the Broncos — and especially the Denver offense — in Week 2. It’s also pretty easy to envision the Broncos corners enjoying a matchup with an average group of receivers. Denver can also put some pressure on Trevor Lawrence, and I trust the defense to do well against a shaky Jacksonville backfield. On top of all of that, the Broncos look rather sharp here. While most of the action on our VSiN betting splits pages shows public faith in Jacksonville, the line hasn’t budged. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards.
